C-RELEASE-WORKFLOW-SIMPLIFY-309.Summary: Simplify release and deployment automation to one explicit, version-neutral GitHub Actions workflow that verifies only release-critical properties and publishes the same offline artifact it installs, updates and rolls back.
C-RELEASE-WORKFLOW-SIMPLIFY-309.Problem: Issue 309 removed the ordinary PR fan-out, but the current release publisher still chains from a separate version-specific gate, polls multiple unrelated workflows, redispatches failed/missing Actions and reruns project/browser tests before building. That is the waiting loop visible to the user and leaves deployment orchestration more complicated than the product risk requires.

Goals.Goal: Replace the release-gate → workflow_run publisher chain with one manual workflow named Release.
Run release verification inside that workflow using native job dependencies rather than GitHub API polling or workflow redispatch.
Execute project check/unit/smoke once and the critical browser suite once for an explicit release attempt.
Build the full offline bundle exactly once, then verify install/update/rollback using that same output before Project Control packaging and GitHub Release upload.
Require exact current main SHA before release work and again immediately before publication.
Keep ordinary PR/main development free from release-scale browser, offline bundle and deployment work.

Constraints.Constraint: The exact base is main 12f93755be01e5f4dccec7b18d418db7ec119abd and issue 309 is reopened until this deployment simplification is merged.
No application/domain behavior, SQLite schema, applied migration, immutable source/evidence, PIN or ACL semantics change.
Release publication is not performed by this change; the workflow is prepared and tested, while an actual GitHub Release still requires an explicit release run from current main.
Production remains Docker-free; Docker is allowed only as the disposable Debian reference environment used by existing offline bundle/systemd verification.
Backup/restore, exact artifact checksum, atomic update and rollback verification remain fail-closed.
No polling loop, gh workflow run recovery, temporary workflow or version-specific release workflow is introduced.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Bump VERSION or publish v0.4.3 in this change.
Modify annual protocol import, parser, UI or storage.
Rewrite the native installer or backup subsystem.
Declare real Astra Linux acceptance complete.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: .github/workflows/release.yml is the single release workflow, is version-neutral and starts only through workflow_dispatch.
.github/workflows/release-gate.yml is removed and README badges/docs point to release.yml.
The release workflow has no workflow_run, push or pull_request trigger and therefore does not run on ordinary development merges.
The release workflow contains no GitHub Actions polling loop, no gh workflow run, no sleep-based waiting for external checks and no automatic redispatch.
Project check/unit/smoke and backup self-test run once in release verification; critical Playwright runs once in the release browser job.
The publisher builds one full offline bundle, passes the same OUT directory to systemd-deploy-selftest.sh, creates Project Control from that verified archive and uploads only the checked assets.
Exact main SHA is verified before heavy publication work and immediately before tag/release creation.
Existing ordinary CI and risk-scoped GRACE remain unchanged; this governed release/CI change passes GRACE final plus the ordinary project check on one exact PR head.
The superseded CI simplification change C-CI-SIMPLIFY-309 is moved to terminal applied archive in the same PR without a separate bookkeeping PR.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: node --test tests/ci-simplification.test.mjs tests/release-workflow.test.mjs tests/release-recovery-workflow.test.mjs tests/release-assets-contract.test.mjs tests/release-0.4.1.test.mjs tests/release-0.4.2.test.mjs tests/docs-consistency.test.mjs
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: One manual Release workflow, no cross-workflow polling/redispatch, one build-once artifact path through deployment verification and unchanged ordinary PR CI.
